metadata.name: SCORE2-OP (Systematic Coronary Risk Evaluation 2 — Older Persons, Age 70–89)
metadata.summary: Estimates 10-year fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular disease risk in older adults aged 70–89 years using competing-risk adjusted Fine-Gray models.
clinical_pearls: Accounts for competing risk of non-cardiovascular mortality in adults aged 70–89 years.
ESC risk thresholds for age >=70 years: <7.5% low-to-moderate, 7.5–14.9% high, >=15% very high.
Includes diabetes as a predictor variable (unlike SCORE2) because diabetes strongly modifies CVD risk in older adults.

Pitfall — Lower discrimination & frailty gap: Discrimination in older adults is modest (C-index 0.63–0.67) compared with SCORE2, and validation is limited in severely frail or multimorbid patients; not intended for established CVD or non-European populations without recalibration.

interpretation.label: Low-to-Moderate Risk (<7.5%)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk <7.5% for adults aged >=70 years. Risk factor pharmacotherapy generally not indicated for primary prevention alone.

interpretation.label: High Risk (7.5–14.9%)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk 7.5% to <15% for adults aged >=70 years. Consider risk factor treatment accounting for frailty and life expectancy.

interpretation.label: Very High Risk (>=15%)
interpretation.summary: 10-year CVD risk >=15% for adults aged >=70 years. Risk factor treatment generally recommended if tolerated.

references.citation: SCORE2-OP working group and ESC Cardiovascular risk collaboration. SCORE2-OP risk prediction algorithms: estimating incident cardiovascular event risk in older persons in four geographical risk regions. Eur Heart J. 2021;42(25):2455-2467.
